reports.text:
Indication: jaundice, right upper quadrant tenderness, elevated transaminases.
Technique: grayscale and color Doppler imaging of the right upper quadrant.
Liver: normal in size and echotexture. No focal hepatic lesion.
Biliary: no intrahepatic or extrahepatic ductal dilatation. Common bile duct 3 mm.
Gallbladder: normally distended, no stones, no wall thickening, no pericholecystic fluid. Sonographic Murphy sign negative.
Portal vein: patent with normal hepatopetal flow.
Pancreas: visualized portions unremarkable.
Right kidney: normal size, no hydronephrosis.
No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Normal right upper quadrant ultrasound. No biliary obstruction.

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital, Emergency Department. Date of visit 06/19/2026, arrived 18:50, discharged 23:40. Faxed to primary care 07/10/2026 on request.

CHIEF COMPLAINT: feeling unwell x1 week, urine dark.

HPI: 35M, generally healthy, about a week of malaise and tiredness. Noticed his urine turning dark, "like tea," over the same week. Some mild nausea, has not vomited. Denies abdominal pain. No fever he has measured. Got back from a work trip to Southeast Asia earlier this month. History of remote IV drug use, none currently. Had hepatitis at 24 which resolved on its own. No acetaminophen beyond a couple of doses, no supplements or herbal products, no new medications.

PMH: IVDU, in remission. Hepatitis age 24, resolved.
MEDS: none.
ALLERGIES: NKDA.
FAMILY HX: father with alcohol use disorder; mother with HTN.
SOCIAL: never smoker. EtOH socially, 1 to 2 per week. International logistics consultant.

ROS: positive as in HPI. Negative for chest pain, SOB, confusion, bleeding or bruising, rash.

EXAM: T 37.3, HR 88, BP 128/78, RR 16, SpO2 98% RA.
Gen: tired-appearing, nontoxic, alert and oriented.
Eyes: sclerae mildly icteric.
CV: regular, no murmur. Lungs: clear.
Abd: soft, nondistended, tender to palpation in the right upper quadrant. Liver not enlarged. No splenomegaly. No ascites.
Skin: no rash, no petechiae, no spider angiomata.
Neuro: nonfocal, no asterixis.

RESULTS:
AST 980 U/L, ALT 1150 U/L, total bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL, alk phos 110 U/L, albumin 4.2 g/dL. INR 1.0. Remainder of CMP and CBC unremarkable.
RUQ US: normal liver, no biliary dilatation, gallbladder normal.
Acute hepatitis panel sent, pending at discharge.

MDM: marked hepatocellular transaminase elevation with mild hyperbilirubinemia, preserved synthetic function (normal INR and albumin), normal mental status, imaging without obstruction. Picture is acute hepatitis, most likely viral given recent travel. Tolerating PO. No indication for admission.

DIAGNOSIS: acute hepatitis, likely viral.

DISPOSITION: home. Avoid alcohol. Limit acetaminophen. Hydrate. Follow up with PCP in 2 to 3 days for repeat labs and serology results. Return for confusion, vomiting and unable to keep fluids down, bleeding, worsening yellowing or abdominal pain.

Electronically signed, ED attending physician.
